page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb is a bare-metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 2288G processor with 8 physical cores and 16 threads running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The platform is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled directly, consisting of 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity.

Performance benchmarks indicate solid mid-tier capabilities. The server achieves average single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, alongside average Passmark CPU scores. Memory performance is highly polarized; while the Passmark memory score ranks in the top tier, large-block memory bandwidth tests show weaker bottom-quartile results. Single-threaded compression and decompression benchmarks, such as gzip and bzip3, demonstrate strong top-quartile performance.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 and substantial local NVMe storage, this server offers a cost-effective bare-metal profile for workloads requiring high resource density without virtualization overhead. It is well-suited for database hosting, memory-intensive caching layers, and static web serving, as evidenced by its average Redis SET throughput and static web serving benchmarks. It is less optimal for larger LLM inference tasks, where prompt processing and text generation benchmarks for 7B models fall into the bottom quartile.
